newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AWB Report-Australia, EU may take new tenders.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AWB Report-Australia, EU may take new tenders.

text.p: Australia and the European Union (EU) appeared more likely than the U.S. to fill latest Pakistan and Egyptian wheat tenders, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said in its weekly grain market report.

Nearby tenders were announced last week by Sri Lanka and Pakistan, with each seeking 100,000 tonnes of wheat for April delivery, AWB said. The Sri Lanka tender was filled by Argentina and the EU, AWB pointed out.
Rumours also circulated last week of Egypt re-entering the market for 500,000 tonnes of wheat for May shipment.
Toward the end of the week Peru bought 25,000 tonnes of hard wheat from Argentina at US$161.00 a tonne fob in one of the few sales transacted in the week, AWB said.
The AWB attributed a settling of U.S. wheat prices toward the end of last week, after a mid-week rise, to a failure by the U.S. to win in international tenders.
The threat of cyclone in the Australian state of Queensland last week had a limited impact on sorghum prices, with local prices again rising by about A$10.00 a tonne over the week.
Sorghum delivered Brisbane ended the week at A$145.00-A$150.00 a tonne and at about A$160.00 a tonne delivered Newcastle, it said.
Continued strength appeared to reflect a lack of grower selling, although some sorghum was making its way into the Victorian market, it said.
In Victoria, dairy demand was showing signs of easing and feed grain cash prices, for barley, triticale and feed wheat, fell by about A$2.00 a tonne over the week.

The AWB confirmed that its wheat shipments in the week ended March 14 totalled 515,626 tonnes, bringing exports so far this shipping year to 8.92 million tonnes. This is far ahead of the 6.02 million tonnes shipped at the same time last year.
